members.reason: ["Outside the shared analysis: EO 6205-C is a section 4(a) interim agreement ('pursuant to Section 4 of the National Recovery Act') that binds five divisions of the Silk Association of America to the Cotton Textile Industry Code from July 17, 1933, 'pending action upon a Code of Fair Competition to be presented by the Silk Association of America', 'subject to cancellation at any time without notice'. SHARED_ANALYSIS item 5 excludes section 4(a) agreements from the analysis, and section 4(a) authority is not shown to have ended with the section 3 code-approval repeal of June 14, 1935 (the shared analysis treats April 1, 1936 as the end of what remained of Title I).", "First end not established: EO 6330 (October 10, 1933, held) approves the Code of Fair Competition for the Silk Textile Industry, which may have replaced the interim agreement, but EO 6330 does not mention EO 6205-C, the Silk Association, its five divisions or the Cotton Textile Industry Code, and nothing held shows that the five divisions fall within the Silk Textile code, when that code took effect, or that the Administrator cancelled the agreement. Sources needed: the Silk Textile Industry code text (scope, effective date) or an NRA notice cancelling the interim agreement."]

["Own-terms end undatable: condition 2 says <<my approval of the Code as a separate Code is limited to a period of three (3) months from the effective date thereof>>, with authority for the Administrator to require the industry to operate under the Graphic Arts Industries code. The order states no effective date and no held text other than EO 6532 names the Photo-Engraving Industry code (full-repository search of jobs/ and research/readiness), so the date three months after the effective date cannot be computed or bounded. Source needed: the Photo-Engraving Industry code text with its effective date (WPA: IV NRA Codes 429) or an NRA notice.", "No held record shows whether the Administrator extended the limit or ordered the industry to operate under the Graphic Arts code (EO 6606-B, February 17, 1934); either decides whether the separate approval ended in 1934 on the three-month limit, was replaced, or ran to the June 14, 1935 repeal. Evidence does not show the event in any interval, so no first end is supportable."]

["First end unsupported: EO 6606-E (February 17, 1934) amends condition 1 of the order of December 23, 1933 approving the Electrotyping and Stereotyping Industry code (EO 6533, held). EO 6533 condition 2 limits that approval 'as a separate Code' to 'a period of three (3) months from the effective date thereof' and authorizes the Administrator to require the industry to operate under the Graphic Arts Industries code. The amended condition exists only as long as the approval it amends; the code's effective date, any extension, and any order requiring Graphic Arts code operation are not held (no held text beyond EO 6533 and this order names the code), so whether the amended condition ended in 1934 or ran to the June 14, 1935 repeal cannot be decided. Source needed: the Electrotyping and Stereotyping code text with its effective date (WPA: VII NRA Codes 623) or a later order."]

["Independent command without an end: after approving the code, the order directs the Division of Research and Planning of the National Recovery Administration to make a study of wages and hours in the industry and submit its report and recommendations to the National Industrial Recovery Board 'as soon as practicable'. It is a direction to an agency, so it needs its own end or block. 'As soon as practicable' is a deadline, not an end, and no held record shows the study made or the report submitted.", "No held text ends the direction: EO 7075 (June 15, 1935) terminated the Board but does not mention the Division of Research and Planning or this direction; EO 7252 (December 21, 1935, effective January 1, 1936) terminated the NRA and transferred only the Division of Review, the Division of Business Cooperation, the Advisory Council and the Consumers' Division, but nothing held shows the Division of Research and Planning still existed then or that the direction lapsed with it, and the owner's 2026-10-28 ruling requires a reason that a later general rule extinguished the command. Source needed: a held record of the study or report, or of the Division's abolition."]
